origin: cwe/89/php Key Principles: bind LIKE wildcard values as a parameter too - concatenating "%$search%" into an otherwise-prepared query still injects the wildcard portion

finding.name: SQL Injection
finding.summary: $term is concatenated directly into the LIKE pattern before prepare() is called, so the prepared statement has no placeholder at all - $term reaches the SQL text unparameterized despite prepare() being called.

trap: Replacing $term with $pdo->quote($term) inside the LIKE clause's SQL text - prepare("... LIKE '%" . $pdo->quote($term) . "%'") - looks like manual sanitization closes the gap, but PDO::quote() already wraps its own output in surrounding quote characters, so concatenating it inside the LIKE clause's existing literal quotes produces a mangled, doubly-quoted pattern rather than a safely delimited one - and PDO's own documentation is explicit that quote() should not be relied on for security with every driver. The fix is to remove $term from the query text entirely: prepare("... LIKE ?") and bind '%' . $term . '%' as the parameter value passed to execute(), never building the wildcard pattern inside the SQL string.
must_preserve: searchProducts still returns products whose name contains $term as a substring match, the same LIKE '%...%' semantics as before. Special SQL characters in $term (quotes, wildcards) do not change the query's structure.
